summary: Lockfile-only change to packages/eql/Cargo.lock. It moves reqwest 0.13.3 -> 0.13.4 and hickory-resolver/hickory-proto 0.25.2 -> 0.26.3, which pulls in hickory-net, prefix-trie, system-configuration, core-foundation 0.9.4 and ndk-context. Several Windows-only crates also shift between windows-sys versions. In this workspace the only path to reqwest/hickory is eql_tests (publish = false) -> cipherstash-client/stack-auth. The published crate eql-bindings does not depend on them, and a library's Cargo.lock does not ship to crates.io consumers. Nothing shipped to customers changes. The realistic failure is a DNS or HTTP behaviour change that breaks the test harness's connection to ZeroKMS. CI ran the e2e property suite, which uses that path, and it passed, as did all 28 check runs including osv-scanner. Impact is low and the change is ready for normal review.

behaviour_changes.description: The DNS resolver stack used by reqwest in the eql workspace moves from hickory 0.25.2 to 0.26.3 (new hickory-net crate, resolver now uses system-configuration on macOS and ndk-context on Android). This removes the versions named in GHSA-q2qq-hmj6-3wpp and GHSA-3v94-mw7p-v465.
reqwest 0.13.3 -> 0.13.4, used by cipherstash-client and stack-auth for ZeroKMS/auth HTTP calls inside the eql_tests harness.

Windows-only dependency edges are re-resolved: errno, rustix, tempfile, quinn-udp and rustls-platform-verifier now lock windows-sys 0.59.0 instead of 0.60.2/0.61.2, and one crate moves to windows-sys 0.48.0. This has no effect on Linux builds.

failure_scenarios.title: hickory 0.26 / reqwest 0.13.4 behaviour change breaks ZeroKMS connectivity in the test harness
failure_scenarios.trigger: The new resolver handles DNS differently (system config, search domains, IPv6 ordering) or reqwest 0.13.4 changes connection behaviour in a given environment.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: cipherstash-client and stack-auth resolve and connect to ZeroKMS through reqwest, which now uses hickory-resolver 0.26.3 with a restructured crate layout (hickory-net split out).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Fixture generation or the e2e property suite fails to authenticate or encrypt, locally or in CI. This is a loud failure in test tooling. No shipped artefact or customer data is involved.

existing_verification.description: The e2e property suite (fresh encryption through ZeroKMS) and the PG17 shards ran on the head commit.

missing_verification: Fixture regeneration (fixture-gen feature) was not shown to have run against the new resolver.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Revert the lockfile change if the harness breaks. No release action is involved.

failure_scenarios.title: Re-resolved windows-sys / macOS system-configuration edges break non-Linux developer builds
failure_scenarios.trigger: A developer builds the eql workspace on Windows or macOS.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The lockfile moves several crates to different windows-sys versions and adds system-configuration 0.7 / core-foundation 0.9.4 for macOS. CI runs only on Ubuntu runners, so these target-specific edges are not compiled there.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A local build fails on a developer machine. This is recoverable by re-locking, and nothing ships.
missing_verification: No macOS or Windows build of packages/eql in the CI results provided.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Cargo only locks versions within each crate's declared range, so breakage is unlikely. Fix by re-locking if reported.

verification_gaps.description: Non-Linux targets are not compiled in the CI results provided, so the target-specific lock edges are unexercised.
